paragraphs.text: When to add molding capacity
Second molding line: reserve, build or buy overflow. Investment committee, January 2027
Pelican Packaging
Investment committee
Synthetic benchmark case; every number from the briefing pack
Executive summary
Do not build now: reserve the slot as a $0.60M option, book the contract molder for 2028, and order the line only once a 2029 service gap and about $3.3M of funding are proven
The line is nearly full, and forecast demand overruns it from 2028, though much of the growth is unsigned
–	2027 demand uses 92% of practical capacity, not the 83% Operations reports
–	Forecast overflow: 0.6M units in 2028, 3.4M in 2030; 0.8M on signed minimums
Building now breaks the cash covenant and buys little that cheaper bought-in overflow cannot provide
–	A January order leaves cash $3.0M below the covenant minimum
–	Bought-in overflow costs less than a line until it passes about 3.1M units
–	The 23% faster growth Sales cites is a cross-section, not proof of cause
The contract molder can bridge overflow through 2029, but 2029 is tight and 2030 needs a second line
–	The molder's cap covers 2028–29 but leaves 26% of 2030 overflow unserved
–	In 2029 just 0.3M units of molder room remain, and none for specialty
Reserve the slot as a capped $0.60M option, and release the $4.2M balance only at a June 2027 gate
–	The slot keeps $1.2M above the floor; the order needs about $3.3M of funding
–	The deposit pays off only if a funded order averts a 2029 fill-rate miss
–	If either test fails in June 2027, cancel and decide 2030 on signed volume
